title: Retention verification metrics (v1) — required signals, SLIs, and alert thresholds
body:
Owner: Caleb Johnson (Observability)
Primary reviewers: Logan Wright (Telemetry), Allison Grant (Obs Standards), Sean Gallagher (SRE)
Last pass aligned with: purge job framework + retention policy evaluator wiring (see linked PRs)

Purpose
- Define the minimum set of metrics required to verify retention enforcement across stores (request/response logs, audit logs, traces/metrics, artifacts where applicable).
- Specify labels, expected cardinality, and alert thresholds suitable for company-wide dashboards (no per-tenant explosions).
- Provide SLIs used for GA readiness gates and for the “Compliance reporting pack” evidence checklist.

Important instrumentation constraints (please read)
- DO NOT label metrics with tenant_id, user_id, request_id, prompt_hash, or any unbounded identifiers.
- Allowed segmentation labels (bounded): store, region, env, tier, job_name, result/status, error_class (bounded), policy_source.
- “job_name” must be from a fixed allowlist (e.g., request_logs_ttl_purge, audit_logs_ttl_purge, traces_ttl_compactor).
- “error_class” must be mapped to a bounded taxonomy (timeout|rate_limited|db_deadlock|validation|dependency|unknown).
- For multi-tenant hosted stores, we rely on aggregate correctness + sampled per-tenant verification via log-based checks (tracked separately). This sheet is metrics-only.

Store taxonomy (label: store)
- request_logs (request/response logs; may be partially disabled by logging mode)
- audit_logs (security audit events)
- traces (distributed tracing spans)
- metrics (time-series metrics retention)
- artifacts (eval datasets / compliance pack artifacts; only where product supports retention)
- policy_service (retention policy evaluation/export service)

Metric table (spreadsheet export)
Columns:
A Metric name | B Type | C Description | D Required labels | E Optional labels | F Expected cardinality | G SLI / how used | H Alert threshold (default) | I Suggested dashboard panel | J Notes

1) redwood_retention_ttl_lag_seconds
- Type: histogram
- Description: Time lag between “record eligible for deletion” (now - retention TTL) and “record actually deleted/expired” for each store.
- Required labels: store, region, env, tier
- Optional labels: policy_source (default|customer|exception)
- Expected cardinality: store(<=6) * region(<=10) * env(<=3) * tier(<=3) * policy_source(<=3) ~ <= 1,620 series per quantile bucket (manageable)
- SLI / how used: Primary SLI for retention enforcement. We track p50/p95/p99 over 1h and 24h.
- Alert threshold (default):
  - SEV2 (page): p95 ttl_lag_seconds > 6h for 30m (hosted/dedicated), > 12h for 60m (private)
  - SEV3 (ticket): p95 ttl_lag_seconds > 2h for 2h (hosted/dedicated)
- Suggested dashboard panel: “TTL lag (p95) by store/region” + “TTL lag (p99) top regions”
- Notes: For stores that expire via partition drop/compaction, emit lag based on compaction watermark.

2) redwood_retention_purge_rows_deleted_total
- Type: counter
- Description: Number of rows/events deleted by purge jobs (or equivalent deletion mechanism), by store.
- Required labels: store, region, env, tier, job_name
- Optional labels: result (success|partial|skipped)
- Expected cardinality: store(<=6)*region(<=10)*env(<=3)*tier(<=3)*job_name(<=12)*result(<=3) ~ <= 6,480
- SLI / how used: Used for sanity checks (deletion happening), and to compute “effective throughput” during backlog incidents.
- Alert threshold (default): none directly; paired with backlog + lag.
- Suggested dashboard panel: “Rows deleted/min (rate) by store”
- Notes: Use monotonic counter; do not emit per-batch gauge.

3) redwood_retention_purge_failures_total
- Type: counter
- Description: Count of purge job failures (hard failures after retries). This is not “attempts”; only terminal failure for an execution window.
- Required labels: store, region, env, tier, job_name, error_class
- Optional labels: dependency (db|object_store|queue)
- Expected cardinality: store(<=6)*region(<=10)*env(<=3)*tier(<=3)*job_name(<=12)*error_class(<=6) ~ <= 38,880 (high but bounded; keep job_name allowlisted)
- SLI / how used: Reliability SLI for purge framework; used to trigger incident response.
- Alert threshold (default):
  - SEV2 (page): rate(purge_failures_total[15m]) > 2 AND ttl_lag p95 is breaching in same store/region
  - SEV3 (ticket): rate(purge_failures_total[1h]) > 1 for any store/region
- Suggested dashboard panel: “Purge failures by error_class”
- Notes: Ensure error_class mapping occurs at source (don’t use raw exception string).

4) redwood_retention_purge_backlog_rows
- Type: gauge
- Description: Estimated backlog rows/events eligible for deletion but not yet deleted (or queued for deletion).
- Required labels: store, region, env, tier
- Optional labels: backlog_source (scan|queue|estimate)
- Expected cardinality: <= store(<=6)*region(<=10)*env(<=3)*tier(<=3)*backlog_source(<=3) ~ <= 1,620
- SLI / how used: Early warning signal; pairs with “rows deleted rate” to estimate time-to-clear.
- Alert threshold (default):
  - SEV2 (page): backlog_rows increasing monotonically for 60m AND ttl_lag p95 > 2h
  - SEV3 (ticket): backlog_rows > 10,000,000 for 4h (tune per store; see notes)
- Suggested dashboard panel: “Backlog size + slope (deriv)”
- Notes: For large stores, absolute thresholds must be store-specific; use ratio-based thresholds where possible.

5) redwood_retention_purge_job_duration_seconds
- Type: histogram
- Description: Wall-clock duration of purge job runs, from start to completion.
- Required labels: store, region, env, tier, job_name
- Optional labels: result (success|partial|failed)
- Expected cardinality: store*region*env*tier*job_name*result ~ <= 6,480
- SLI / how used: Capacity/efficiency; detects stuck jobs.
- Alert threshold (default):
  - SEV3 (ticket): p95 duration > 20m for 2h (any job), or p99 duration > 60m for 30m
- Suggested dashboard panel: “Purge job duration (p95) by job_name”
- Notes: Keep job window sizes consistent to make duration comparable.

6) redwood_retention_purge_job_last_success_timestamp_seconds
- Type: gauge
- Description: Unix timestamp of last successful completion for each purge job.
- Required labels: store, region, env, tier, job_name
- Optional labels: none
- Expected cardinality: store*region*env*tier*job_name ~ <= 2,160
- SLI / how used: “Heartbeat” for scheduled jobs.
- Alert threshold (default):
  - SEV2 (page): now - last_success > 2h (hosted/dedicated core stores: request_logs, audit_logs)
  - SEV3 (ticket): now - last_success > 6h (other stores)
- Suggested dashboard panel: “Last success age (minutes) by job”
- Notes: Use this instead of “up” checks where scheduling is async.

7) redwood_retention_deletion_verification_mismatches_total
- Type: counter
- Description: Count of verification checks that found records older than retention TTL still present (sampled queries / watermark validation).
- Required labels: store, region, env, tier
- Optional labels: verification_method (sample_query|watermark|partition_check)
- Expected cardinality: store*region*env*tier*method ~ <= 1,620
- SLI / how used: Correctness SLI. This is the customer-trust signal and supports compliance evidence.
- Alert threshold (default):
  - SEV2 (page): rate(mismatches_total[30m]) > 0 for request_logs or audit_logs (hosted/dedicated)
  - SEV3 (ticket): rate(mismatches_total[6h]) > 0 for other stores
- Suggested dashboard panel: “Verification mismatches (rate) by store”
- Notes: Verification should be read-only and low-QPS. If verification is disabled in Private, document that as N/A in reports.

8) redwood_retention_policy_eval_latency_seconds
- Type: histogram
- Description: Latency of retention policy evaluation (control plane path) including cache hits/misses.
- Required labels: env, region
- Optional labels: cache (hit|miss), outcome (ok|error)
- Expected cardinality: env(<=3)*region(<=10)*cache(<=2)*outcome(<=2) ~ <= 120
- SLI / how used: Ensures policy service doesn’t become bottleneck; impacts enforcement correctness if errors.
- Alert threshold (default):
  - SEV3 (ticket): p95 > 250ms for 2h
  - SEV2 (page): error rate > 1% over 15m
- Suggested dashboard panel: “Policy eval latency + cache hit rate”
- Notes: Errors must be separately counted (see next metric).

9) redwood_retention_policy_eval_errors_total
- Type: counter
- Description: Errors in policy evaluation (validation failures, dependency failures).
- Required labels: env, region, error_class
- Optional labels: dependency (db|cache|kms)
- Expected cardinality: env*region*error_class ~ <= 180
- SLI / how used: Reliability; should be near-zero.
- Alert threshold (default):
  - SEV2 (page): rate(errors_total[15m]) > 5
- Suggested dashboard panel: “Policy evaluation errors by class”
- Notes: Any sustained errors risk falling back to defaults; ensure fallback behavior is logged and included in compliance pack narrative.

10) redwood_retention_policy_change_events_total
- Type: counter
- Description: Count of retention policy changes (create/update/delete) written to audit trail.
- Required labels: env, region
- Optional labels: change_type (create|update|delete), actor_type (human|service)
- Expected cardinality: env*region*change_type*actor_type ~ <= 360
- SLI / how used: Not an SLI; used for auditing and to detect unexpected churn.
- Alert threshold (default):
  - SEV3 (ticket): spike detection (e.g., > 20 changes in 10m) for prod
- Suggested dashboard panel: “Policy changes over time”
- Notes: Do not include actor_id label.

11) redwood_retention_legal_hold_active
- Type: gauge
- Description: Whether a legal hold is active for a tenant scope (aggregate only).
- Required labels: env, region, tier
- Optional labels: hold_type (legal|incident)
- Expected cardinality: env*region*tier*hold_type ~ <= 180
- SLI / how used: Report annotation; explains why deletions may pause.
- Alert threshold (default): none; informational.
- Suggested dashboard panel: “Active holds by tier/region”
- Notes: In hosted, do NOT expose tenant-level holds in metrics; surface in audit logs and compliance pack.

12) redwood_audit_exporter_events_exported_total
- Type: counter
- Description: Number of audit log events exported via the audit-log-exporter (used for compliance pack exports).
- Required labels: env, region
- Optional labels: template (baseline|customer_custom), result (success|failed)
- Expected cardinality: env*region*template*result ~ <= 120
- SLI / how used: Ensures exporter works; paired with exporter failures.
- Alert threshold (default): none.
- Suggested dashboard panel: “Audit exporter throughput”
- Notes: Template is bounded; do not allow arbitrary template ids as labels.

13) redwood_audit_exporter_failures_total
- Type: counter
- Description: Export failures (pack generation failures, missing event types, time-window query errors).
- Required labels: env, region, error_class
- Optional labels: stage (query|render|bundle|upload)
- Expected cardinality: env*region*error_class*stage ~ <= 360
- SLI / how used: Report-pack operational health.
- Alert threshold (default):
  - SEV3 (ticket): rate(failures_total[1h]) > 0
  - SEV2 (page): rate(failures_total[15m]) > 3 during business hours (Mon–Fri)
- Suggested dashboard panel: “Compliance export failures by stage”
- Notes: Tie to CS/SecEng runbook; many of these become customer-visible.

14) redwood_retention_compliance_pack_generation_latency_seconds
- Type: histogram
- Description: Time to generate baseline compliance report pack (end-to-end) including exports and attachments.
- Required labels: env, region
- Optional labels: result (success|failed)
- Expected cardinality: env*region*result ~ <= 60
- SLI / how used: Customer expectation SLI for enterprise reviews.
- Alert threshold (default):
  - SEV3 (ticket): p95 > 30m for 1d
  - SEV2 (page): p95 > 60m for 4h (prod)
- Suggested dashboard panel: “Compliance pack generation latency (p95)”
- Notes: This is for the generator service; not the UI download.

Store-specific notes / tuning guidance
- request_logs: Expect highest volume. Backlog absolute thresholds should be higher; rely more on ttl_lag. SEV2 paging tied to p95 lag breach.
- audit_logs: Lower volume but high importance. Any verification mismatch is a SEV2.
- traces/metrics: Many backends enforce retention via compaction windows. Use watermark-based verification where possible.
- artifacts: Only instrument if artifacts are stored in a system with purge semantics (object store lifecycle + delete verification). If retention is “customer-managed only” in Private, mark N/A.

SLO targets (initial proposed, subject to rollout)
- Hosted/Dedicated:
  - TTL lag p95 <= 60 minutes (steady state) for request_logs and audit_logs
  - TTL lag p95 <= 6 hours (worst-case during incidents/maintenance; breach pages)
- Private:
  - Default SLOs are “best effort” unless contractually defined; still page on hard failures for managed components.

Alert routing (SRE)
- SEV2 pages to: #oncall-sre + #oncall-telemetry (per region rotation)
- SEV3 tickets to: ENG-Observability backlog + tag owners by store:
  - request_logs: Logan Wright
  - audit_logs/exporter: Kevin Osei
  - policy_service: Jordan Lee / Ethan Park

Open questions / TODO
- Confirm per-store backlog thresholds after we get 2 weeks of prod baseline.
- Decide whether we need a separate metric for “purge job throttled” vs “skipped due to safety limits” (currently result=skipped).
- Private deployments: document which metrics are guaranteed to exist when customer runs external telemetry stack.

Change log
- 2025-01-22: Initial draft created (Caleb)
- 2025-02-11: Added policy_service + exporter metrics for compliance pack (Kevin/Caleb)
- 2025-03-12: Tightened cardinality guidance; added last_success heartbeat gauge (Allison/Sean feedback)
